correctness.rationale: The source Eq. (5) discriminant has sign kappa(u-theta), and Eq. (11) reduces exactly to y_next=rho Wy+eta action with zero prejudice coupling. The pair-constant invariant subspace yields u_H=eps/D and u_L=1-eps/D; when b<theta<1-b, exact strict best responses switch the two groups and the affine update interchanges H=1-rho*eps/D and L=rho*eps/D. H>L because eta>0. Row stochasticity gives norm-infinity contraction rho<1 on each sign cell; positive margins force a neighborhood of the orbit to remain in alternating sign cells, yielding an attracting period-two orbit, and strictness plus inversion of I-rho^2 W^2 ensures admissible robustness. The standalone standard-library Fraction verifier evaluated all 4-player coefficients from the original map, both exact iterates, signed rational discriminants, influence eigenvectors and multipliers, and consensus fixed points from the newly produced file. No finite enumeration substitutes for proof.

originality.rationale: The claim is the model-specific, parameter-open attracting two-cycle for the exact four-agent public-goods/Friedkin–Johnsen map of arXiv:2604.08840v1 with its synchronous Assumption 1 update. The source explicitly permits full simultaneous updating but conjectures convergence to an equilibrium in Section IV. Full primary text contains no such period-two construction. The closest 2023 and 2025 opinion–action models use coordination/anti-coordination instead of this constant-cost public-goods payoff; the 2016 synchronous threshold-game example shows that generic two-cycles are known, but does not imply the claimed strict four-dimensional orbit on a primitive weighted graph. Searches of relevant published mathematical result summaries and primary literature revealed no dominating theorem or exact match. A preprint-versus-later-version difference and incompleteness of global search remain stated residual risks; no uniqueness or priority guarantee is claimed.

value.rationale: The target preprint explicitly leaves convergence to equilibrium as a conjecture across update sequences permitted by its Assumption 1, and its distinct all-defection theorem holds only on a special sufficient parameter regime. A completely explicit stable switching attractor shows that universal convergence fails even with complete primitive social influence, so network connectedness and aperiodicity alone cannot repair the conjecture. Its strict rational gap and parameter openness rule out fragile tie-breaking, and simultaneous-update policy is a directly motivated structural boundary for the coevolutionary social-dilemma model. No significance claim is made for generic synchrony-induced oscillations, already known, or for real-world empirical prediction.
